text: Arvind Kejriwal, born on 16 August 1968 in Siwani, Bhiwani district of Haryana, to Gobind Ram Kejriwal and Gita Devi, is an Indian politician, activist, and former bureaucrat who served as the 7th Chief Minister of Delhi from 2013 to 2014 and from 2015 to 2024. He is the national convener of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) since 2012 and represented the New Delhi constituency in the Delhi Legislative Assembly from 2013 to 2014 and again from 2015 to 2025. Kejriwal, a mechanical engineer from IIT Kharagpur, worked in the Indian Revenue Service (IRS) from 1995 until his resignation in February 2006. In 2006, he was awarded the Ramon Magsaysay Award for Emergent Leadership for his role in the Parivartan movement, which used the Right to Information (RTI) Act to combat government corruption. He founded the Public Cause Research Foundation in December 2006 with Manish Sisodia and Abhinandan Sekhri, using his award prize money as seed funding, and later launched the AAP in November 2012 to fight corruption and improve governance. In the 2013 Delhi Legislative Assembly elections, AAP won 28 seats, with Kejriwal defeating incumbent Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit in New Delhi by 25,864 votes, forming a minority government with support from eight Indian National Congress MLAs, one Janata Dal MLA, and one independent MLA. He became the second-youngest Chief Minister of Delhi on 28 December 2013. On 14 February 2014, he resigned after failing to pass the Jan Lokpal Bill, citing opposition from the Indian National Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party, and later admitted he had made a mistake in not explaining his resignation publicly. In the 2015 Delhi Legislative Assembly elections, AAP won 67 out of 70 seats, securing a decisive majority, and Kejriwal was re-elected from New Delhi by a margin of 31,583 votes. He was sworn in as Chief Minister for the second time on 14 February 2015. In 2020, AAP won again, retaining power in Delhi, and Kejriwal was sworn in for a third term. The party also won a major victory in the 2022 Punjab Legislative Assembly election. In 2024, Kejriwal was arrested on 21 March by the Enforcement Directorate on allegations of a liquor scam involving the AAP-led Delhi government, becoming the first sitting chief minister in India to be arrested. His party leaders, Satyendra Jain, Sanjay Singh, and Manish Sisodia, also spent months to years in jail without bail, trial, or conviction. The opposition alliance accused the arrest, made weeks before the 2024 Indian general election, of being a case of fabrication and "match-fixing" by the BJP, with Amnesty International stating that financial and terrorism laws were weaponised against political opponents. On 10 May 2024, the Supreme Court ordered Kejriwal's release on interim bail until 1 June 2024 due to his election campaigning. He surrendered at Tihar Jail on 2 June 2024 and was granted bail by the Supreme Court on 13 September 2024 with certain conditions, though the case continues. On 17 September 2024, Kejriwal resigned as Chief Minister, stating he would only return as CM if he received a public mandate. In the 2025 Delhi Legislative Assembly election, AAP suffered a heavy defeat, with Kejriwal losing his New Delhi seat to Parvesh Verma by a margin of over 4,000 votes, along with many other notable party members. Kejriwal was involved in the Parivartan movement, which began in December 1999 and focused on exposing corruption in public distribution, public works, income tax, and electricity through RTI applications, leading to the exposure of a PDS scam in 2003 and 2008, and the stalling of a World Bank water privatisation project in 2004. In 2005, he and Manish Sisodia launched Kabir, a registered NGO focused on RTI and participatory governance. Kejriwal also led the India Against Corruption (IAC) movement in 2011, demanding a strong Jan Lokpal Bill, which was eventually passed by the Delhi Assembly in 2015. During his tenure, AAP established Mohalla Clinics, primary health centres, with 187 clinics set up by 2018 serving over 2 million residents, and a target of 1,000 clinics by 2020. In October 2019, New Delhi began offering free bus transit for women on the Delhi Transport Corporation.

Issues related to the distribution of governmental responsibilities and public appointments have been a point of contention, with Manish Sisodia describing the situation as "a battle between the selected and the elected" and indicating that after a legal setback, the government was prepared to take the matter to the Supreme Court of India. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government established Mohalla Clinics—primary health centres—in Delhi starting in 2015, with 187 such clinics operational by 2018, serving over 2 million residents. The government had set a target of establishing 1,000 Mohalla Clinics before the 2020 Delhi Legislative Assembly Elections. These clinics provide free essential health services, including medicines, diagnostics, and consultations, serving as the first point of contact for residents and reducing referrals to secondary and tertiary facilities. Beginning in October 2019, New Delhi introduced free bus transit for women on the Delhi Transport Corporation using pink tickets with a message from Arvind Kejriwal. Kejriwal has faced criticism for controversial remarks on Biharis and "outsiders." The Shunglu Committee submitted a report to the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi raising concerns about government decisions. AAP won 62 out of 70 seats in the 2020 Delhi Legislative Assembly election, and Arvind Kejriwal took oath as chief minister on 16 February 2020 at Ramlila Maidan, matching Sheila Dikshit’s record. On 21 March 2024, he became the first sitting chief minister in India to be arrested and imprisoned. After being released on bail by the Supreme Court, he vowed to resign on 15 September 2024 to campaign for the upcoming Delhi assembly elections and formally resigned on 17 September 2024, with education minister Atishi Marlena named as his successor. During the April 2021 COVID-19 pandemic, the Congress accused the Kejriwal government of spending heavily on publicity campaigns while failing to increase oxygen storage or build new oxygen plants. A central government-appointed committee criticized the AAP-led Delhi government for using state funds for advertisements promoting Kejriwal and his party, allegedly violating Supreme Court guidelines. In response to an RTI query, it was revealed that funds were allocated in December 2020 for eight oxygen plants, only one of which was completed, with the remaining funds diverted to advertising. During the oxygen crisis in 2021, the central government increased oxygen allocations to Delhi, prompting Kejriwal to publicly thank them for providing 730 tons of oxygen, though critics accused him of being "criminally liable" for patient deaths due to shortages. In July 2022, a Supreme Court-appointed audit panel found that the Delhi government had exaggerated its oxygen requirements by four times during the second wave. On 30 March 2022, the official residence of Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal was attacked by a group of BJP supporters during a protest, with Manish Sisodia alleging it was part of a conspiracy to murder Kejriwal. AAP MLA Saurabh Bhardwaj filed a petition in the Delhi High Court seeking a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the attack, claiming the incident involved "tacit complicity" by the Delhi Police, including breaches of security, damage to property, and vandalism while police failed to intervene. On 31 March 2022, eight individuals were arrested, and charges under provisions related to obstructing public servants and damaging public property were filed. The Delhi High Court noted inadequate security arrangements and sought a status report from the Delhi Police. Kejriwal was arrested on 21 March 2024 by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) after skipping nine summons, following the Delhi High Court’s rejection of his anticipatory bail in connection with the Delhi liquor policy money laundering case, making him the first sitting chief minister in India to be arrested while holding office. The opposition alliance called the case a fabricated one and "match-fixing" ahead of the 2024 general elections. The Delhi High Court dismissed Kejriwal’s petition against arrest and all bail requests, and the Supreme Court granted him interim bail from 10 May 2024 to 1 June 2024 for campaigning purposes. After the end of interim bail and failure to extend it on medical grounds, Kejriwal surrendered at Tihar Jail on 2 June and remained in judicial custody until 5 June 2024. A Delhi court denied a plea for seven-day interim bail, extending custody until 19 June and then to 3 July 2024. On 20 June 2024, Kejriwal was granted bail by the trial court on a bail bond of 100,000 INR, though his release was delayed as the ED appealed. He was then questioned for three days by the CBI and arrested on 26 June 2024 from Tihar Jail in the same case, remaining in judicial custody until 12 July. On 12 July 2024, the Supreme Court granted interim bail in the money laundering case related to the alleged excise policy scam, but he remained in jail due to the CBI arrest. On 5 September 2024, the Supreme Court reserved its order on his bail, which was pronounced on 13 September 2024, granting him bail and leading to his release from Tihar Jail after five months, though he served more than five months in prison. Kejriwal discusses corruption and Indian democracy in his book Swaraj, advocating for decentralisation, panchayat involvement in local decisions and budgets, and criticizing foreign multinational corporations' influence and central politicians' lack of accountability. In 1995, Kejriwal married Sunita, a 1993-batch IRS officer, who voluntarily retired in 2016 as Commissioner of Income Tax in the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal. The couple has a daughter and a son; Kejriwal follows Hinduism, is a vegetarian, practices Vipassanā meditation, and is diabetic. He underwent surgery in 2016 for a persistent cough. Kejriwal identifies as an Ambedkarite and calls himself a 'devotee' of B. R. Ambedkar. In May 2021, Kejriwal called for India to stop air travel between India and Singapore and develop "vaccine alternatives for children" due to a "new variant of coronavirus found in Singapore" said to be dangerous for children. However, the Singapore Health Ministry stated there was no known Singaporean variant; the reported threat discussed a variant first detected in India (B.1.617), and the ministry rejected the assertions as false. Indian and Singaporean foreign ministers criticized Kejriwal’s comments as "irresponsible" and "counter-factual" respectively. In 2022, a central government panel accused the Kejriwal government of inflating Delhi’s reported oxygen needs during the second wave of the pandemic. Several defamation cases were filed against Kejriwal by political opponents. In January 2014, Kejriwal released a list of corrupt politicians, including Nitin Gadkari, who filed a defamation suit; Kejriwal later apologized to Gadkari and Kapil Sibal. In 2016, Kejriwal made allegations against Bikram Majithia, then Punjab revenue minister, over drug trade, leading to a defamation case; Kejriwal apologized in March 2018. Kejriwal also made allegations against finance minister Arun Jaitley regarding DDCA irregularities, leading to a Rs 5-crore defamation suit; on 2 March 2016, the Delhi High Court asked Kejriwal and Kirti Azad to file written statements, and in April 2018, Kejriwal and three others apologized jointly to Jaitley. In his affidavit to the Election Directorate before the 2015 elections, Kejriwal declared 10 criminal charges and 47 total charges against him. In 2021, a Delhi court dismissed an assault case filed by a bureaucrat against Kejriwal and ten AAP MLAs, finding no prima facie case. In February 2024, Kejriwal was involved in a defamation lawsuit and issued an apology to the Supreme Court for retweeting a 2018 YouTuber Dhruv Rathee video on the BJP IT Cell. On 11 March 2025, a Delhi court ordered an FIR against Kejriwal for allegedly misusing public money on large hoardings. In late April 2023, the BJP alleged Kejriwal misappropriated public funds for renovating his residence, prompting an investigation announced on 29 April 2023; the CBI initiated an investigation into funds spent on renovating Kejriwal’s residence, with the Vigilance Department pursuing allegations of misappropriation and financial irregularities. In March 2014, a leaked video showed Kejriwal instructing journalist Punya Prasun Bajpai on promoting his interview by comparing his resignation to Bhagat Singh’s sacrifice and dropping content on privatisation to appear anti-middle class; when the interview aired, Bajpai was found to have complied, leading to accusations of "media fixing." Kejriwal was arrested on 21 March 2024 by the ED on allegations of a Delhi liquor scam involving the AAP government, accused of spying on ED officials and having skipped nine ED summons; the Delhi High Court dismissed his petition against arrest. He was granted bail by the Delhi High Court on 20 June 2024, though release was delayed due to an ED appeal. His ministers, Satyendra Jain and Manish Sisodia, were also in jail without bail or conviction, with Satyendra Jain spending over two years in jail and Manish Sisodia granted bail by the Supreme Court on 9 August 2024. The opposition alliance labeled the arrest as "fabricated" and "match-fixing" before the 2024 general elections; Amnesty International stated financial and terrorism laws were weaponized against political opponents, while the BJP denied any political motive. An Insignificant Man is a 2017 Hindi/English socio-political documentary co-produced and directed by Khushboo Ranka and Vinay Shukla, co-produced by Anand Gandhi, covering the rise of anti-corruption protests and the formation and rise of the Aam Aadmi Party and Arvind Kejriwal. Kejriwal has appeared on news talk shows and interviews, spoofing himself on the third episode of The Viral Fever’s Barely Speaking With Arnub, where actor Jitendra Kumar cosplayed as him, and also appeared in Kunal Kamra’s YouTube interview series Shut Up Ya Kunal.
